summary: The analyze prompt adopts the persona 'You are a Scrum Development Team following Agile Best Practices.' Output includes a Quality signal (Ready/Questions/Blocked), explicit Blocker vs Question distinction (blockers prevent Quality=Ready; questions are carried forward), and technology questionnaires offering Rigging-derived concrete options (e.g. flask/django/fastapi for Python web).
title: Analyze agent persona: Scrum team with role-based surfacing and Quality signal

rationale: HTML allows rich formatting without a templating framework. QuarterDeck already supports path_html via the document renderer. Storing state in METADATA.md keeps it in a plain text file commands can read/write without parsing the display artifact.
summary: The Captain's Chair is a self-contained HTML file (captains_chair.html) registered in console.yaml as a document item with path_html, rendered by QuarterDeck in an 80vh iframe. Each drydock command fills a Rigging HTML template with variables and writes it forward-only. Lifecycle state is tracked in target-root METADATA.md via 'drydock build state:' field (ladder: init→analyzed→planned→building→built). Commands only overwrite the Chair when the new state is forward of the current.
title: Captain's Chair is self-contained HTML; lifecycle state in METADATA.md

affected_scope: analyze, metadata, manifest, cli, prompts, Rigging
rationale: Design ratified in notes_analyze.md V4: PO-centric decomposition where LLM proposes and human ratifies; quality signal replaces opaque verdict; lifecycle advances forward-only to prevent regression.
summary: Rewrote drydock analyze: Scrum team persona (6 roles), new ANALYSIS.md format with Blocked/Questions/Ready quality signal and story list, BUILD_CONFIGURATION.md injection, COMPASS unpopulated detection, lifecycle state in METADATA.md, Captain's Chair template, manifest.py work graph (ManifestNode, ManifestGraph, parse/render, frontier, story cap).
title: Analyze pipeline redesign — Scrum team persona, quality signal, lifecycle, manifest graph

rationale: The generic ideas cards could not express the approved first-page SAIL presentation cleanly in HTML or print output.
summary: Documentation assembly now supports a dedicated SAIL cover section with oversized S, A, I, and L letterforms paired to grouped copy from specification frontmatter.
title: Add SAIL cover layout to documentation renderer

rationale: Design session established that section should be the item home, not its workflow stage. Actions is a derived state driven by pending review or questionnaire completion. No rejected state — rejection keeps item pending in Actions.
summary: Implemented home-based section routing (pending items surface in Actions regardless of declared section), two-state nav icon boxes (red X / green check), new page header (title + filename + Approve button + divider), single-format document rendering (html>pdf>md priority), and four-section layout (Core/Actions/Docs/Archive). Removed build_plan section; board moved to Core.
title: QuarterDeck nav, routing, and page header redesign

alternatives.option: Keep seeding the full corpus and have analyze ignore it
alternatives.reason_rejected: Leaves drift artifacts in blueprint/ and contradicts source-of-truth model

rationale: Observed defect: blueprint/ was polluted with ARCHITECTURE.md/DATABASE.md/FEATURE-Example.md/etc. at import time, contradicting the Arrange-pipeline model where typed spec files are plan create outputs and COMPASS is analyze's output. METADATA.md remains at the target root as the forward-only lifecycle anchor for set_build_state.
summary: drydock import (markdown/source/speckit) no longer copies the typed-spec template corpus into blueprint/. It now seeds only root identity files (METADATA.md, README.md) via init_specification(root_identity_only=True). After import, blueprint/ contains only sources/; COMPASS.md is an analyze output and typed spec files are plan create outputs.
title: import seeds only root identity; blueprint holds only sources

rationale: Drydock needs a repeatable in-repo workflow for prompt critique instead of ad hoc chat reviews, with durable artifacts and comparable scores across iterations.
summary: Added drydock prompt review to evaluate prompt contracts against the spec, matching notes, and consumer contracts with deterministic scoring and archived review artifacts.
title: Add prompt review workflow

rationale: The previous section mixed command scopes, led with quality details before command purpose, and implied a fixed questionnaire model that conflicts with the approved analyze design notes.
summary: Reorganized the SAIL Phase 2 section to present analyze, QuarterDeck review, and plan creation in execution order, and clarified that questionnaires and spikes are driven by actual unresolved decisions rather than a fixed set.
title: Clarify SAIL Phase 2 specification flow

rationale: Import is the intake boundary for analyze and plan create, so removing it from the user-facing Phase 2 flow made the specification incomplete.
summary: Restored drydock import to the SAIL Phase 2 specification after it was accidentally omitted from the prior reorganization.
title: Restore import to SAIL Phase 2 flow

rationale: The public import flag for seeding COMPASS.md is compass, not intent. The specification must use the actual command surface consistently.
summary: Replaced the stale drydock import --format intent references in the Drydock specification with drydock import --format compass.
title: Rename import compass format in specification

rationale: The init scaffold should contain only baseline target state. Creating an empty board artifact at init time adds noise and implies plan state before any plan exists.
summary: Drydock init no longer creates QuarterDeck/tickets.json; the board file is created later by plan generation when executable work exists.
title: Stop creating QuarterDeck tickets during init

alternatives.option: Bake ANALYSIS.html via an analyze post-processor
alternatives.reason_rejected: Couples analyze to presentation and relies on html>md precedence; a config-driven render type is simpler and reusable

alternatives.option: Stuff analysis sections into the Captain's Chair
alternatives.reason_rejected: Overloads the scoreboard; ANALYSIS deserves its own artifact

rationale: Gives the analyze stage its own navigable surface alongside the Captain's Chair scoreboard, reusing an existing runtime capability with no new code path, and keeps the opt-in declarative in console.yaml so other structured artifacts can adopt it later.
summary: The init console template declares a file-existence-gated ANALYSIS item using the runtime's tabs:true markdown rendering, which splits the file's ## sections into switchable tabs. Tabbed rendering is config-driven per item, not hardcoded to a filename.
title: Surface ANALYSIS as a tabbed QuarterDeck Core artifact

affected_scope: QuarterDeck board lifecycle and init scaffold
rationale: An empty board during the analyze stage is noise and contradicts the file-existence visibility rule; the analyze stage already drives action through spikes and BLOCKERS.
summary: init no longer creates an empty tickets.json; plan create is the sole writer. The kanban board therefore obeys file-existence visibility and stays hidden until a plan exists (stage 4).
title: Stop seeding tickets.json at init

alternatives.reason_rejected: Does no decomposition and ignores the prompt; contradicts the spec

rationale: The spec and notes_plan.md agree that plan create authors the Blueprint; the deterministic generator neither authored specs nor ran the prompt, leaving the prompt unwired. Wiring the prompt with module-side parsing, state-merge, and an integrity gate aligns implementation with the approved design.
summary: drydock plan create now implements the reviewed analysis: a single LLM call authors the typed Blueprint spec files (rewriting imported sources per the analyze story map), emits the one BUILD_PLAN_COMPASS.md build-ordering file, and a draft MANIFEST.md. The module merges prior block states, runs a deterministic integrity gate, and writes the QuarterDeck projection. Replaces the prior deterministic 1:1 file-to-story generator.
title: plan create becomes LLM-driven Blueprint authoring

rationale: Two conflicting definitions (curated inventory vs ordered batch file) existed across prompt and notes_plan.md; build needs one ordering contract.
summary: BUILD_PLAN_COMPASS.md is the single build-ordering file: an ordered list of authored spec file names, #-delimited into no-cross-stack build batches, emitted by plan create and consumed by build. Supersedes the prior 'curated inventory' wording.
title: BUILD_PLAN_COMPASS.md has one definition

rationale: Self-hosting analyze produced a 'gaps' questionnaire that asked the human to supply work the team itself derives (which gates are mandatory, what proves self-host, which smoke checks), conflating team analysis with PO decisions.
summary: analyze.md V6 adds an Ownership test: a spike may only ask a decision the team cannot make from the sources. Acceptance criteria, success evidence, smoke checks, build gates, and test sequences are now synthesized outputs, not questions. Dropped the 'gaps / acceptance criteria' spike topic.
title: Constrain analyze spikes to human-owned decisions

alternatives.reason_rejected: No defined format or writer; superseded by feedback files + answered spikes
Non-deterministic LLM output makes id-keyed state merge unreliable

evidence: tests/test_analyze.py, tests/test_planning_session.py — 95 passed; full suite 484 passed
rationale: Iterating a generative step needs persistent human steering separate from the machine artifact. BUILD_CONFIGURATION.md had no spec, format, or value. LLMs are non-deterministic, so preserving plan state/ids across re-plans is not worth the complexity.
summary: analyze and plan create each export a persistent, human-owned feedback file (ANALYSIS_FEEDBACK.md, MANIFEST_FEEDBACK.md) re-injected near the top of the prompt on every run (created if absent, never overwritten). BUILD_CONFIGURATION.md is retired from both prompt stacks and code. The analyze Rigging catalog now injects a filename list (BRA*.md + stack/*.md, no README.md) instead of README content. plan create becomes a single-directional clean regenerate: no existing-MANIFEST injection, no state merge. Integrity gate hardened: >=1 AC per story and ~100-story cap are now fatal.
title: Standing-directive feedback loop; retire BUILD_CONFIGURATION.md

evidence: docs/Drydock_Specification.md section: The QuarterDeck — Agile Development Console
rationale: Spec is the target architecture and diverged from ratified design and shipped behavior recorded in docs/notes_quarterdeck.md; reconciled both spec and the lagging seed template.
summary: Rewrote the canonical spec QuarterDeck section to the implemented configuration-driven console: console.yaml index, blockers/core/actions/docs/archive taxonomy, home-based routing with two-state icons, editable_markdown page type, standard page header (EDIT/APPROVE, no reject), BLOCKERS.md artifact, tickets.json not seeded at init, tabbed Analysis as a Core artifact. Reconciled standard_artifacts.py seed sections to the same taxonomy (board and manifest feedback moved to Core; project_pages renamed docs; build_plan removed).
title: QuarterDeck specification synced to ratified console.yaml model

rationale: Gives the reader a defined persona while keeping the document a normative third-person specification; resolves mixed marketing/tutorial voice and product-owner/Commander inconsistency.
summary: The specification defines The Commander as the product-owner persona that directs the build, addresses the reader by that role, and writes in third-person present tense throughout (no second-person 'you', first-person 'we/our', or future tense).
title: Establish The Commander as the canonical operator persona

rationale: Drydock needs executable benchmark fixtures and machine-readable evidence to verify the specification-driven process instead of relying on prose-only review.
summary: Added a repo-local validation harness with three benchmark cases, deterministic scoring, and report aggregation under validation/.
title: Add validation benchmark scaffold

evidence: docs/Drydock_Specification.md Workspace Layout matrix; docs/notes_quarterdeck.md Artifact Feed Matrix
rationale: An artifact is only worth keeping if it feeds a command forward or backward; making producer/consumer relationships an explicit contract removes guesswork and prevents ghost artifacts and stray injections.
summary: A files-by-commands matrix declares, for every workspace artifact, which command produces (O), consumes (I), gates on (X), or produces-if-absent (O*) it. Applied to the authoritative spec at the top of the Workspace Layout section. SOUNDINGS gains plan create O/I (reads to reproject).
title: Artifact Feed Matrix governs artifact producer/consumer routing

alternatives.reason_rejected: Superseded — lives apart from the prompt and must be kept in sync; the header is co-located and symmetric with output:

evidence: src/drydock/prompts.py render_inputs/input_tokens; prompts/analyze.md, prompts/plan_create.md inputs: rows; commit 634bacd
rationale: Matrix enforcement must be configuration, not hardcoded assembly logic; the prompt header is the right home, symmetric with the existing output: row, so adding or re-routing an input is a config edit.
summary: Each LLM-assisted command declares its consumed artifacts and injection order in an ordered, COMPASS-first inputs: row in its prompt frontmatter, derived from the Artifact Feed Matrix. analyze and plan create assemble prompts by iterating prompt.input_tokens through a shared render_inputs dispatch; reordering the row reorders the prompt. Single files named by filename; globbed groups use suffix-less tokens (QUESTIONNAIRES, TYPED_SPEC).
title: Agent inputs declared in prompt frontmatter inputs: row

evidence: QuarterDeck/app.py; docs/SOUNDINGS.md QD-012; tests/test_quarterdeck.py buttonless tests
rationale: The two-path resolution buttons were nonsensical to the Commander and data was lost on tab switch; answered-equals-has-text plus autosave matches normal local-web-app behavior and the answered-subset already drives plan create.
summary: Spike and non-spike questionnaires render with no resolution buttons (the former Implement as Story / Commander Implements and Save Answers are removed). A question is answered iff its field holds text; answers autosave on field blur (state=answered) without reload, so tab switches never lose data. Only answered fields feed downstream; partial questionnaires are valid.
title: QuarterDeck questionnaires are buttonless with autosave

alternatives.reason_rejected: Redundant given writeback; dual-write was the anti-pattern
Would require changing LLM injection path; file-per-item is simpler

rationale: SQLite was an anti-pattern: questionnaire state was already canonical in .json files via writeback. Approve/AC were implemented without design backing. One source of truth per file, injected as-is into LLM prompts.
summary: Removed console_state.sqlite and all DB code from app.py. Questionnaire answers written back into .json source files. Archive flag embedded as 'archived' field in questionnaire JSON. Non-questionnaire archive state is session-scoped. Removed approve/decision and AC verification — never part of the design.
title: Remove SQLite from QuarterDeck; replace with file-based state

rationale: Duplicating the same questions in ANALYSIS.md tabs and QuarterDeck action items created redundant review work and ambiguity about where answers belong.
summary: drydock analyze no longer persists an Open Questions section in ANALYSIS.md; nonblocking questions are surfaced only as QuarterDeck questionnaire action items, and answered or existing questions must not be duplicated.
title: Questionnaires are the analyze question surface

rationale: A Claude execution bypassed the writer by editing target files and returned a narrative summary instead of the required delimited MANIFEST block.
summary: Plan creation now disables Claude tools, preserving the text-only artifact contract, and separates streamed provider progress messages.
title: Harden plan-create LLM output boundary

rationale: Claude produced complete planning artifacts as tool-call transcripts despite its no-tools invocation, causing valid output to be discarded.
summary: drydock plan create recovers Blueprint, BUILD_PLAN_COMPASS.md, and MANIFEST.md artifacts when Claude returns non-executed Write-call XML instead of delimited blocks.
title: Plan create recovers simulated Write artifacts

alternatives.reason_rejected: Does not identify executable story groups, initial conditions, or prompt budgets

rationale: A flat specification inventory cannot prepare the incremental, context-bounded build sequence required by drydock build.
summary: Plan creation now requires BUILD_PLAN_COMPASS.md to define ordered, testable story groups with initial conditions first and per-step context and token-budget estimates.
title: Compass defines token-budgeted build groups

rationale: User confirmed the old format (blueprint/code_root/status/type/Agent Instructions) was not intentional design. build_dir is the correct concept for where built code lands, distinct from the Drydock target directory.
summary: METADATA.md now uses a clean flat format (name/display_name/short_description/stack/version/build_dir) without legacy fields. get_build_dir() replaces get_code_root(), resolving --build-dir arg → METADATA.md field → DRYDOCK_BUILD_DIRECTORY/<Target>.
title: Standardize METADATA.md format and build_dir resolution

rationale: User prefers sonnet for build (many per-story calls, cost matters). Frontmatter defaults were being used as authoritative which prevented user-level override without editing prompt files.
summary: LLM model resolves via CLI --model arg, then DRYDOCK_MODEL env var (set via drydock config set drydock_model), then defaults to sonnet. Prompt frontmatter model: field is a hint only and is ignored at runtime.
title: Model config hierarchy: --model → DRYDOCK_MODEL → sonnet

rationale: Instructions at the end of context is the correct LLM prompt engineering pattern — model reads context before receiving its task directive.
summary: All LLM-assisted commands assemble prompts as: job-block (scalar context) → render_inputs() (content) → prompt body (instructions). Previous analyze implementation had body first, which was a bug. Now corrected.
title: Prompt assembly order: job-block → inputs → body (instructions last)

rationale: METADATA.md was blank after init for most fields. Commands had the data but never wrote it back. Sync keeps project identity and lifecycle state current without requiring manual edits.
summary: render_metadata now emits all 13 fields with blank defaults. Added set_field, increment_version, stamp_last, set_sub_state, copy_metadata_to_build_dir. drydock_build_state renamed to build_state with legacy migration. analyze pre-flights short_description and stack prompts; backfills stack from LLM summary; stamps last_analyzed. plan create increments version, advances build_state to planned, stamps last_planned. import_source writes detected stack when field is empty.
title: METADATA.md lifecycle sync implemented
